considered_not_added.reason: refuted/retracted: Vogt et al. 2010 36.6 d claim not recovered; tied to activity by Robertson et al. 2014; absent from von Stauffenberg et al. 2024 3-planet solution. exoplanet.eu and OEC: Retracted.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 581 f
considered_not_added.reason: refuted/retracted: Vogt et al. 2010 433 d claim not recovered by later HARPS/CARMENES analyses (von Stauffenberg et al. 2024: no residual signal). exoplanet.eu and OEC: Retracted.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 581 TESS 3.12 d TLS peak
considered_not_added.reason: Not a planet claim: von Stauffenberg et al. 2024 (Sect. 4.5, Fig. 6) found a 3.12 d TLS peak in TESS Sector 51 near planet e's period and concluded it is a marginal false-positive detection.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 3138 candidate P=1.05d (alias 20.4d)
considered_not_added.reason: Not claimed as a planet: Astudillo-Defru et al. 2017b Sect. 4.2.1 -- FAP 0.9%, BIC does not favour the extra Keplerian, and 20.4 d is half the rotation period; authors 'interpret that this low RV signature is possibly provoked by stellar activity'.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 3138 48.2 d RV signal
considered_not_added.reason: Activity: anti-correlated with H-alpha, modelled as an RV-H-alpha correlation (Astudillo-Defru et al. 2017b Sect. 4.2.2).

considered_not_added.name: GJ 3998 316 d RV/FWHM sinusoid
considered_not_added.reason: Activity cycle, not a planet claim (Stefanov et al. 2025 abstract: 'long-term sinusoidal imprints in RV and FWHM of period 316 d').

considered_not_added.name: GJ 367 52.2 d RV signal
considered_not_added.reason: Activity: rotation (Goffo et al. 2023 Sect. IV; indicators peak at 48-54 d).

considered_not_added.name: TOI-270 Dynamite-predicted planets (P~1.84 d, ~21 d)
considered_not_added.reason: Pure statistical prediction from Kepler-based architecture models (Turtelboom et al. 2025, AJ 170, 3, Tables 3-4); no detected signal.

considered_not_added.name: LHS 1678 astrometric companion (P ~ 42 yr fit)
considered_not_added.reason: Authors' own classification is brown dwarf: Silverstein et al. 2022 (AJ 163, 151) Sect. 7.3/App. C -- 'likely a brown dwarf', every mass combination they simulate (P = 42 or 100 yr, photocentric a = 17 or 100 mas) gives a brown dwarf, though they 'cannot yet eliminate the possibility that it is a Jovian planet'; Silverstein et al. 2024 call it 'the brown dwarf companion'. No mass is actually measured, so the >13 MJup rule is met only by the authors' inference. WRITER'S JUDGEMENT: could instead go on the Rejected tab as 'unlikely'.

considered_not_added.name: LHS 1678 Dynamite-predicted planets
considered_not_added.reason: Statistical predictions only (Turtelboom et al. 2025, AJ 170, 3, Tables 3-4), no detected signal.

considered_not_added.name: Wolf 1061 67.27 d signal (Wright et al. 2016 'd')
considered_not_added.reason: refuted as a planet: Astudillo-Defru et al. 2017b (A&A 602, A88, Sect. 4.5) -- 2.5% FAP, near a 64 d H-alpha peak and a 66 d window-function peak, 'we do not regard the 67-day signal as a planet detection'; Tuomi et al. 2019 App. A.39 -- 'no evidence' for it. The letter d now belongs to the 217 d planet.

considered_not_added.name: LP 791-18 e (exoplanet.eu, P=1.65 d)
considered_not_added.reason: Pure statistical prediction, no detected signal: Turtelboom et al. 2025 (AJ 170, 3), Dynamite v3 PCM prediction table (Table 3); exoplanet.eu nonetheless lists it as a transit 'Candidate' with alias TOI-736 e. There is no TOI-736.03 in the NASA TOI table.

considered_not_added.name: Teegarden's Star 96 d signal
considered_not_added.reason: Stellar rotation (Dreizler et al. 2024 abstract; Lafarga et al. 2021).

considered_not_added.name: Teegarden's Star ~2500 d variation
considered_not_added.reason: Seen in RVs and activity indices; authors suggest an activity cycle (Sect. 6, App. F). Not a planet claim.

considered_not_added.name: HD 189567 18.6 d residual
considered_not_added.reason: Not claimed: FAP ~2.5% and only weak Bayesian evidence (ln O < 2) for 3- or 4-planet models; Unger et al. 2021 Sect. 5.5: 'the 18.6-day signal is not significantly detected'.

considered_not_added.name: HD 189567 61 d signal
considered_not_added.reason: Activity: same period in the FWHM; removed by FWHM detrending (Unger et al. 2021 Sect. 5.5).

considered_not_added.name: HD 134060 hidden 2:1 planet at 1.65 d
considered_not_added.reason: Tested and disfavoured by Bayesian model comparison (Delta BIC 3.1 circular, 23.5 eccentric); Udry et al. 2019 Sect. 5.7. A hypothesis, not a signal.

considered_not_added.name: HD 60532 hypothetical terrestrial planets
considered_not_added.reason: Dynamical stability study only, no detected signal (arXiv:1304.1563).

incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.item: YZ Cet b period on the confirmed tab is 1.96876 d (Astudillo-Defru+2017). Stock et al. 2020 (A&A 636, A119) resolved the alias to 2.02087 d; NASA pscomppars (2.02087 d) and Mignon et al. 2024 Table 4 (2.02101 +/- 0.00005 d) agree. The confirmed-tab row (and any a_au derived from it) looks outdated.

GJ 433 c (confirmed tab, 5094 d) is not secure: Feng et al. 2020 (ApJS 246, 11) list it among the 'eight planet candidates ... which need to be confirmed', and Tuomi et al. 2019 (arXiv:1906.04644, App. A.29) find no long-period signal without the UVES data and attribute it to a UVES barycentric bias. NASA lists it as confirmed (disc. Tuomi+2014). The writer may want a caveat on the confirmed-tab row.

GJ 3998 b and c (confirmed tab): Dodson-Robinson et al. 2022 (arXiv:2201.13342) find high RV-activity coherence at both periods and say they 'may actually be stellar signals'; Stefanov et al. 2025 (arXiv:2503.08405) confirm both with more HARPS-N data. Contested, not refuted.

GJ 180 c (confirmed tab, 24.33 d, Tuomi et al. 2014): Feng et al. 2020 (ApJS 246, 11, Sect. IV.2) report 'the 24-day [signal] in T14 is not found to be significant'; Mignon et al. 2024 (A&A 689, A32, Table 4) recover only GJ 180 b. Tuomi et al. 2019 still recover it. NASA lists it confirmed. Contested; the writer may want a caveat.

Wolf 1061 d on the confirmed tab has P = 67.27 d (Wright et al. 2016). That signal was rejected (Astudillo-Defru et al. 2017b; Tuomi et al. 2019); planet d is the 217 d signal (NASA pscomppars 217.21 d, Msini 7.70 M_E; Mignon et al. 2024 217.914 +/- 0.305 d). The row's period (and any a_au derived from it) should be updated; the 7.70 M_E mass already matches the 217 d solution.

HD 134060 c: confirmed tab has P = 1160.9 d; the discovery paper (Udry et al. 2019, A&A 622, A37, Table 11) and NASA pscomppars give 1291.56 +48.0/-44.2 d. The 1160.9 d value matches exoplanet.eu and OEC. Worth checking which the sheet should carry.

GJ 1061 b, c, d: Mignon et al. 2024 (A&A 689, A32, Sect. 7.4.3) could not recover any published GJ 1061 signal from their homogeneous HARPS reduction because of an unexplained seasonal RV offset. They do not dispute the planets; noted for completeness.
